reference.insight_principle: BJ Fogg's Behavior Model: When ability is blocked (broken interaction), motivation crashes regardless of trigger strength. Without immediate feedback, users assume failure and disengage.
reference.insight_text: User clicked 'Add to cart' three times in rapid succession (3.4 seconds) without scrolling or viewing product details, suggesting the button is unresponsive or cart feedback is missing.
reference.recommendation: Implement instant visual feedback on cart button click: loading spinner, success animation, and slide-in cart preview.

reference.insight_principle: Hick's Law and Choice Overload Effect (Schwartz, Iyengar) - decision time increases logarithmically with number of choices, leading to paralysis and abandonment when options lack clear differentiation
reference.insight_text: User rapidly clicked through multiple categories (Tech→Wearables→Bags) within 3 seconds, then immediately navigated back to Home and Shop.
reference.recommendation: Implement a guided discovery flow: add a prominent 'Help me find' quiz/filter above category buttons.

reference.insight_principle: Hick's Law & Choice Paradox: Increased options and decision complexity exponentially increases decision time and abandonment.
reference.insight_text: User increased cart quantity twice then immediately removed all items within 1.7 seconds. Zero scroll depth on cart page suggests no review of shipping costs or trust signals before abandoning.
reference.recommendation: Implement a cart-level micro-commitment intervention: 'Save for Later' button with real-time social proof.

reference.insight_principle: Commitment & Consistency (Cialdini) — Once users begin a sequence of small commitments, they follow through to maintain psychological consistency with their initial decision.
reference.insight_text: User executed a perfect linear checkout flow in 53 seconds with zero hesitation signals.
reference.recommendation: Implement post-purchase upsell modal BEFORE 'Back to store' redirect showing complementary products.

reference.insight_principle: Commitment & Consistency (Cialdini) - Once users take small steps, they follow through with progressively larger commitments to remain consistent with their initial action.
reference.insight_text: User progressed through the entire checkout funnel in just 4 seconds with zero hesitation signals.
reference.recommendation: Analyze this successful conversion pattern; A/B test reducing steps by combining 'Continue to payment' and 'Review order'.

reference.insight_principle: Information Scent Theory (Pirolli & Card): Users follow cues that promise desired information. When scent goes cold immediately, users backtrack.
reference.insight_text: User spent 64 seconds on page but showed zero scroll engagement before immediately clicking back to store.
reference.recommendation: A/B test hero section with pattern interrupt: replace static hero with dynamic social proof ticker.

reference.insight_principle: Commitment & Consistency (Cialdini) + Cognitive Dissonance: User made micro-commitments but encountered something at checkout that violated expectations.
reference.insight_text: User reached checkout page but immediately exited back to 'Shop' after clicking 'Proceed to checkout' — classic cart abandonment pattern.
reference.recommendation: Implement one-click checkout preview BEFORE the checkout page.

reference.insight_principle: Information Foraging Theory (Pirolli & Card): Users quickly assess information scent and abandon pages when the cost of continued search exceeds expected value.
reference.insight_text: User spent 187 seconds but only scrolled 39% before clicking the logo/brand link, indicating disorientation.
reference.recommendation: Implement a sticky value proposition bar in the top 20% of viewport.

reference.insight_principle: Hick's Law and Choice Overload (Iyengar & Lepper) - decision time increases logarithmically with number of choices, leading to analysis paralysis.
reference.insight_text: User clicked through 5 navigation elements in just 4 seconds, indicating category overwhelm rather than purposeful exploration.
reference.recommendation: Implement guided shopping quiz ('Find Your Perfect Match') as primary CTA above category navigation.

reference.insight_principle: Hick's Law & Analysis Paralysis: Increased choice complexity exponentially increases decision time and reduces conversion likelihood.
reference.insight_text: User spent 6.9 minutes on page with 100% scroll depth but only 3 clicks, all navigation-focused.
reference.recommendation: Implement progressive disclosure with 3-5 curated product recommendations above-the-fold.

reference.insight_principle: Cognitive Dissonance Reduction: When users oscillate between adding/removing quantity, they are experiencing internal conflict between desire and perceived cost.
reference.insight_text: User added an item quickly, then adjusted quantity up and immediately back down, signaling price sensitivity or commitment anxiety.
reference.recommendation: Introduce a persistent value reinforcement nudge in the cart (free shipping threshold, trust badge).

reference.insight_principle: Price Anchoring: Consumers use the first price they encounter as a reference point for value judgments.
reference.insight_text: Visitor spent the entire 6-second session viewing above-the-fold content, repeatedly dwelling on the 19.99 RSD price before clicking 'Shop Now'.
reference.recommendation: Add a brief value-reinforcing reassurance directly beneath the 'Shop Now' CTA.
reference.estimated_lift: +8-14% CTR to product page with intent retention

reference.insight_text: Visitor spent nearly all 49 seconds on just two section views with zero scroll, suggesting the hero content did not create enough pull to drive exploration.

sessions.scenario_note: Two-product comparison via normal navigation (product page -> back to collection -> different product -> back -> revisit the first product), with deliberate, unhurried dwell time on each (seconds, not milliseconds), ending in an unresolved exit. No event names or labels the comparison explicitly; it must be inferred from the view-A / view-B / revisit-A pattern, matching the real event vocabulary and shape used by this client (click with tag/text, section_view and hover with tag/text/durationMs, exit_intent). A good insight should recognize this as comparison/evaluation between two specific alternatives, not generic choice overload, and should NOT default to FRICTION or BOUNCE_RISK given the deliberate pacing.

Three-way category comparison: visitor opens three different backpacks one at a time from a collection page, dwelling several seconds on each product's section before going back, then deliberately revisits the first item at the end (a callback comparison move). No cart/wishlist action at all, no rapid-fire thrashing. Targets the same gap as constructed-comparison-01 but via a collection-page pattern (product A vs B vs C) rather than a single product's own compare link, and ends on a revisit rather than an exit, to see if the model still reads this as comparison rather than HIGH_INTENT or plain ENGAGEMENT.
